title: Ephemeral lease revocation and priority preemption for soft regional failover
author: Aisha Banerjee
release_notes: Adds ephemeral lease revocation and priority-based preemption to reclaim transient capacity under overload; opt-in via config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled; improved observability (ephemeral_lease_acquire/revoke metrics) and a safety window to avoid user-visible request failures.
description:
Context and motivation: During recent regional overload incidents we observed noisy long-running low-priority requests occupying ephemeral slots and preventing short-lived high-priority traffic from meeting SLOs. This PR introduces an ephemeral lease revocation mechanism plus a priority preemption policy that reclaims ephemeral capacity with a soft handoff (preempt-with-grace) to preserve SLOs while minimizing client errors. Motivation is to reduce tail latency and error rate for priority traffic during capacity pressure without hard-evicting user KV caches or dropping active model state.

What this PR does (single-line sections but continuous): Implements a lease manager (ephemeral_lease_manager) that issues timeboxed leases for ephemeral allocations; adds a lease revocation RPC to allow schedulers to request a graceful drain; introduces a preemption policy that ranks requests by priority and age and uses a configurable "preempt window" (default 200ms) to ask lower-priority leases to yield; integrates the protocol into region_coordinator so reclaim decisions can be region-aware and avoid cross-region instability; exposes metrics and traces for lease acquire/revoke and preemption decisions; provides a small docs how-to and an optional canary manifest for rollout.

Checklist and rollout plan: - [x] Unit tests for lease manager state transitions - [x] Integration tests for revoke handshake and graceful drain - [x] E2E canary job (regression and SLO smoke tests) - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Feature gate config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled=false by default; canary enables true - Rollout: enable in single region as canary for 48 hours, monitor ephemeral_lease_revoke_rate, p95 latency for high-priority traffic, and error_rate; if regression, flip gate off and rollback.

Commits (high-level summary): commit 1 - add lease proto and manager skeleton; commit 2 - implement revoke handshake and graceful stop path; commit 3 - introduce priority preemption algorithm + tests; commit 4 - integrate with region_coordinator and expose metrics; commit 5 - docs, canary manifest, CI pipeline updates; commit 6 - follow-up test fixes and flake fixes.

Files changed (high level): - allocator/ephemeral_lease_manager.go: main state machine and lease book - scheduler/preemption_policy.go: algorithm implementing age/priority ranking and preempt window - runtime/lease_protocol.proto: revoke Acquire/LeaseExpired messages - region_coordinator.go: decision logic to prefer local soft-preempt over remote failover - metrics/ephemeral_leases.prom: new counters/gauges for observability - docs and tests: canary + integration.

Design notes and rationale: We intentionally chose a soft-revoke flow instead of immediate eviction to reduce broken in-flight KV/state for long-running streams. The preemption decision uses a score = priority_weight * priority + age_weight * (1 / age_ms) to avoid starvation and to prefer reclaiming recently-started low-priority allocations. A configurable grace window allows providers/SDKs to finish small critical sections; if the client does not yield within the grace window the runtime falls back to a hard revoke which preserves capacity but is counted as a user-facing failure and emitted to metrics.

Observability and alerts: New metrics: ephemeral_lease_acquire_total, ephemeral_lease_revoke_requested_total, ephemeral_lease_revoke_succeeded_total, ephemeral_preempt_hard_failures_total. New tracing span: lease.revocation.{request,ack}. Added dashboard rows keyed by region and priority-class. Alert: if ephemeral_preempt_hard_failures_total > 5/min during canary, autoswitch gate to false and page SRE.

Testing notes: Integration tests simulate mixed priority traffic and assert that high-priority token p95 reduces by >= 15% under controlled reclaim scenarios. E2E canary (regression job) runs in dev region with feature gate and validates no more than 1% increase in 99th error rate for low-priority workloads.

Review conversation (high-level): Miguel Torres: "Can we avoid revoking leases for streams that report active tool-use?" Response (Aisha): "Added an exemption hook: lease manager now checks a stream_activity marker (best-effort) before hard-revoke; documented behavior in examples." Samir Patel: "Preemption score formula seems sensitive to weight tuning; can we add per-tenant overrides?" Response (Aisha): "Added config.allow_tenant_weights with safe defaults; kept global defaults for canary." Ruth Kim: "CI flake on revoke path (race) — failing test observed." Response (Aisha): "Addressed race by adding a small jitter in the revoke ack path and a targeted unit test; reran CI." CI: initial pipeline failed lint in telemetry parser; fixed Python lint and re-ran — all checks passed.

Backward compatibility and safety: The feature is behind config.ephemeral.preempt_enabled=false; default runtime behavior unchanged. Lease proto adds a new optional field 'grace_ms' and will be ignored by older nodes; region_coordinator will fallback to non-preempt behavior when communicating with older control-plane peers. No breaking API changes.

Canary results summary (post-merge): In the dev canary region after 48h with the gate enabled for a narrow cohort, high-priority p95 latency improved by 18% during injected overload windows. Hard revoke failures remained under 0.3% of revokes due to the grace window. No cross-region failovers observed. We consider this ready for controlled roll out to two additional regions.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Miguel and Ruth. Follow-ups: ENG-9127 on per-tenant weighting dashboard; operational runbook note added to SRE handbook.
